rationale: No matching assumption in WE-020; judged from the text: a $15,000 grant against the cost of qualifying (24 months in the home, declarations) for a pool of about 18,000 first-time buyers a year, with 20,000 grants funded.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-1: prices under the cap rise by less than the grant, because many buyers in the segment get no grant and some supply responds.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-4: some renters at the margin buy sooner because of the grant (the deposit binds first-time buyers).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-2: the supply of homes under the cap responds slowly (approval 12 to 24 months, construction 9 to 15).

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-20: while supply is slow, owners of homes under the cap have clearly fewer alternatives than first-time buyers, who can keep renting, wait, buy above the cap or buy in Lowen.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-2: the supply of homes under the cap responds slowly.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-3: buyers, sellers and builders expect the grant to last at least through Year 4.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-7: couples can arrange title or partner declarations so that a prior owner's household qualifies (declaration-based partner check, no register outside Tamberlay).
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-17: owners, builders and agents can organize to lobby at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-5: first-time buyers knew of the grant from March and could delay.

No matching assumption in WE-020; judged from the text: first-time buyers in a three-year window are mostly households that would buy within a few years anyway; the text gives no sign that the window creates buyers who never would.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-020 (illustrative figures), A-9: some recipients receive job offers in the first 24 months that would require moving.
